questions.statement: Look at the clock: the short hand is on 3 and the long hand is on 12. What time is it?
questions.context: En el salón de un colegio de Manizales hay un reloj de manecillas encima del tablero.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This reads the long hand as the hour; the short hand on 3 shows the hour.
Incorrect. For half past three the long hand must be on 6, not on 12.
Incorrect. For two o'clock the short hand must be on 2, but it is on 3.
Correct. The short hand shows the hour, 3, and the long hand on 12 means o'clock.

questions.explanation: En un reloj de manecillas, la manecilla corta ("short hand") marca la hora y la larga ("long hand") marca los minutos. Si la corta está en 3 y la larga en 12, decimos "It's three o'clock" (las tres en punto).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question do you ask to know the time?
questions.context: Simón está en el parque de Pereira y quiere saber si ya es hora de volver a casa.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "What day is it?" asks for the day of the week, not the time.
Incorrect. "How old are you?" asks for a person's age.
Incorrect. This question asks about rain, sun or wind, not the time.
Correct. "What time is it?" is the question we use to ask the time.

questions.explanation: Para preguntar la hora decimos "What time is it?" (¿qué hora es?). "What day is it?" pregunta el día, "How old are you?" pregunta la edad y "What's the weather like?" pregunta por el clima.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The clock says 7:30. How do you say it in English?
questions.context: El reloj digital de la cocina en Cartagena marca 7:30 cuando Laura sale al colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Seven o'clock is 7:00; this answer forgets the thirty minutes.
Incorrect. Quarter past seven is 7:15, which is fifteen minutes, not thirty.
Correct. Thirty minutes after seven is half past seven.
Incorrect. Half past eight is 8:30; the hour on the clock is seven.

questions.explanation: Cuando pasan 30 minutos de la hora decimos "half past" (y media). Entonces 7:30 es "half past seven". "Quarter past" son 15 minutos (y cuarto) y "o'clock" significa en punto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "I go to bed at nine o'clock at ___."
questions.context: Andrés cuenta su rutina en un audio para su primo que vive en Estados Unidos.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Nine o'clock in the morning is school time, not bedtime; also we say "in the morning".
Correct. We go to bed at night, so we say "at nine o'clock at night".
Incorrect. Noon is twelve o'clock in the middle of the day, so it cannot be nine o'clock.
Incorrect. Monday is a day of the week, and we say "on Monday", not "at Monday".

questions.explanation: Para decir a qué hora nos acostamos usamos "at night" (en la noche): "I go to bed at nine o'clock at night". "Noon" es el mediodía, las doce, y "in the morning" es la mañana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "Sebastian gets up at 6:00 a.m. He has lunch at 12:30 p.m. He does his homework at 4:00 p.m." What does he do at four o'clock in the afternoon?
questions.context: Sebastian vive en Cali y escribe su horario de un día de colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. He gets up at 6:00 a.m., in the morning, not at four in the afternoon.
Correct. The text says he does his homework at 4:00 p.m., four in the afternoon.
Incorrect. He has lunch at 12:30 p.m., not at 4:00 p.m.
Incorrect. The text does not say when he goes to bed, and it is not at four in the afternoon.

questions.explanation: "p.m." se usa para las horas después del mediodía. Las 4:00 p.m. son las cuatro de la tarde, y a esa hora Sebastian hace la tarea ("does his homework"). Las 6:00 a.m. son de la mañana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The clock says 10:15. Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: El partido de fútbol del recreo en un colegio de Barranquilla empieza a las 10:15.

options.feedback: Correct. Fifteen minutes after ten o'clock is quarter past ten.
Incorrect. Quarter to ten is 9:45, fifteen minutes before ten.
Incorrect. Half past ten is 10:30, which is thirty minutes after ten.
Incorrect. Ten o'clock is 10:00; this answer forgets the fifteen minutes.

questions.explanation: Un cuarto de hora son 15 minutos. "Quarter past ten" es 10:15 (las diez y cuarto) y "quarter to ten" es 9:45 (un cuarto para las diez). Hay que fijarse en "past" (después) y "to" (antes).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "School starts at 7:00 a.m. Maria arrives at half past seven." Is Maria on time?
questions.context: En un colegio de Santa Marta las clases empiezan a las siete de la mañana.

options.text: No. She is late; she arrives thirty minutes after school starts.
options.feedback: Correct. Half past seven is 7:30, thirty minutes after 7:00, so she is late.

options.text: Yes. She arrives at seven o'clock.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says she arrives at half past seven, which is 7:30, not 7:00.

options.text: No. She is early; she arrives thirty minutes before school starts.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 7:30 is after 7:00, so she is not early but late.

options.text: Yes. Half past seven is before seven o'clock.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Half past seven, 7:30, comes after seven o'clock.

questions.explanation: Las clases empiezan a las 7:00 y Maria llega a las 7:30 ("half past seven"). Llega 30 minutos después, entonces llega tarde ("late"). "On time" significa a tiempo y "early" significa temprano.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses a.m. or p.m. correctly?
questions.context: La profesora de un colegio de Tunja pide escribir oraciones sobre la rutina con a.m. y p.m.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 7:00 p.m. is in the evening; breakfast is in the morning, so it needs a.m.

options.text: I go to bed at 9:00 a.m.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 9:00 a.m. is in the morning; bedtime at night needs p.m.
Correct. Dinner is in the evening, and p.m. is for times after midday.
Incorrect. 12:30 a.m. is after midnight; lunch at midday is 12:30 p.m.

questions.explanation: "a.m." se usa desde la medianoche hasta el mediodía y "p.m." desde el mediodía hasta la medianoche. La cena ("dinner") es en la noche, por eso "7:00 p.m." es correcto. El desayuno sería a.m.
questions.subject: ingles
